decision_brief.authoring_note: Written from scratch for the 2026-10-02 snapshot after the full fresh recollection (see evidence/recollection/), including the newly captured Oct 1 ISM and claims releases; no sentence is carried over from the 2026-10-01 brief.
decision_brief.headline: October's first data day leaned hawkish: ISM held expansion at 54.5 but prices-paid spiked to 77.9, claims stayed low at 197k, and the street's October-hike chatter (media-reported above 70% per CME FedWatch — not verifiable from here) hardened — with our own direct pricing still dark. September payrolls at 08:30 ET today is the adjudicator.
decision_brief.summary: Both central banks remain on hold — Fed 3.75-4.00% into Oct 27-28, BoC 2.25% into Oct 28 — and the verifiable contracts still sit just off policy: ZQV26, the October 30-day Fed funds contract, closed 96.1150 on Oct 1, implying a 3.885% October monthly (30-day) average EFFR, +1.0 bp over the 3.875% range midpoint; CRAU26's quote side (mid 97.64625, last print 97.6475 on a deeper 69-lot/1,070-volume day) implies roughly 2.354% quarterly average CORRA, about +10.4 bp over target. Neither is a meeting probability and CME FedWatch returned HTTP 403 again, so no direct single-meeting distribution exists in this snapshot — the >70% October-hike odds reported by AlphaPilot (citing FedWatch) are attributed context, not verified data. The new information is in the data: September ISM Manufacturing came in at 54.5 (0.3 under the 54.8 consensus) with prices-paid jumping 6.8 points to 77.9 and employment up 1.5 to 52.7 — inflation pressure re-accelerating even as output slows; weekly claims held at 197k (below the ~201k consensus, prior 198k), so labor is not cracking into Friday. On the tape, the long end steadied (TLT -0.09% on the day) after two heavy weeks (-2.15% w after -3.33% w), oil complex names rallied (XLE +1.95%), and gold firmed (GLD +0.50%). The read: patience with a live hawkish tail; today's payrolls is the week's one genuine swing factor.

what_is_priced.fed: ZQV26 closed 96.1150 on Oct 1: an implied 3.885% October monthly (30-day) average EFFR, +1.0 bp over the 3.875% midpoint of the 3.75-4.00% target range. The contract averages almost the whole month before the Oct 28 decision, so it measures October's starting regime, not the meeting's outcome. Separately, media coverage (AlphaPilot, Oct 1, citing CME FedWatch) reports market-implied odds of another hike on Oct 28 above 70% — a third-party figure this environment cannot verify (direct FedWatch requests return HTTP 403); it is context, carried as such.

The long end has been selling hard (TLT -2.15% w after -3.33% the prior week; media note 30-year yields at multi-decade highs) — a hot payroll compounds duration pain from an already elevated base.
Hike tail: if the street's Oct-28 hike odds (media-reported, unverifiable here) harden further, the Oct/Dec front-end complex reprices faster than a monthly-average proxy reveals.
The BoC hawkish column is still empty by absence, not by evidence: a strong September LFS or a trade rebound on Oct 6/9 removes the dovish lean with no new BoC communication.

fed.stance: Hold at 3.75-4.00% — hike tail alive; no verifiable meeting distribution
fed.rationale: The Sep 16 FOMC raised the target range 25 bp to 3.75-4.00%; that completed action is not itself an October surprise. FedWatch returned HTTP 403 again, so no single-meeting distribution exists in this snapshot and none is estimated; a media-reported >70% October-hike odds figure is attributed context only. ZQV26 closed 96.1150 on Oct 1, implying a 3.885% October monthly (30-day) average EFFR — +1.0 bp over the 3.875% midpoint — but its average is set almost entirely before the Oct 28 decision, so it prices the pre-decision regime, not the meeting. October 1's US data cut hawkish on balance: ISM prices-paid spiked 6.8 points to 77.9 with employment up (headline a mild miss), and claims held near lows at 197k; against that, the cooling JOLTS (-256k) and soft Michigan sentiment keep the dovish side alive.

boc.stance: Hold at 2.25% — growth soft, hawkish column empty by absence
boc.rationale: The Sep 2 decision held the overnight target at 2.25%, with the next decision Oct 28 alongside the MPR. With no weighted hawkish card, the Canadian rope reads dovish by absence rather than on positive evidence; July retail (-0.7% headline) and July GDP by industry (0.0%, essentially unchanged) keep the growth picture flat-to-soft, and August LFS employment fell 41.7k. CRAU26's quote side (mid 97.64625) implies roughly 2.354% quarterly average CORRA, about +10.4 bp above target, and the contract carries a deeper executed print (last 97.6475; 69 trades; volume 1,070); it spans the Oct 28 and Dec 9 decisions and cannot be decomposed into either.

A decomposition of the quarterly CORRA contract into meeting-dated legs would make the October decision tradeable.

decision_brief.trade_status_rationale: Deliberate abstention, not an absent view. Neither board has a verifiable single-meeting distribution (FedWatch 403 again) and the verifiable contracts sit just off policy — the October Fed average +1.0 bp over the midpoint, CORRA futures about +10.4 bp over target — so there is no dislocated price to trade. The asymmetry worth watching runs both ways: inflation pressure re-accelerating (ISM prices 77.9; core PCE 3.0% y/y; Michigan expectations 4.6%) against cooling labor (JOLTS -256k) — with Friday's payrolls the adjudicator and the media-reported hike-odds figure context we cannot verify and therefore cannot size on.
